admin.title: Import a forum
admin.intro: Migrate an existing forum into Flarum. Pick your source platform, connect to its database, test it, then run the import in the background — it processes in batches with a live progress bar, so even large forums won't time out.
admin.dump_help: A mysqldump .sql (optionally gzipped) or a SQLite file. Very large forums may exceed your host's upload limit — use the live connection instead, or gzip the dump first.
admin.upload_failed: Upload failed — the file may be too large for this server's upload limit.
admin.confirm_start: Start importing now? This writes discussions, posts and members into this forum. Import into a fresh forum for best results.
admin.shared_note: Runs in small batches straight from your browser — no queue worker or SSH needed, so it works on shared hosting. Keep this tab open; if it's interrupted, reopen this page and it resumes where it left off.

sync.title: Keep the old forum in sync
sync.messages_only_intro: Content from {source} cannot be synced yet, but its private messages can be brought across: messages between members who were imported, added once each, however many times you run it.
sync.intro: Your {source} import can be brought up to date. A sync copies only what the old forum has gained since — new members, discussions and replies, and edits where {source} records them — and never touches anything written here.
sync.password_help: The password is never stored after a run, so enter it again.
sync.upload_help: This import came from an uploaded file. Upload a fresh dump of the old forum to sync from it.
sync.confirm: Bring across what the old forum has gained since the last run? Content written on this forum is left as it is.

redirects.title: Keep the old links working
redirects.intro: Your old forum's addresses are in Google, in bookmarks, and in every post that ever linked to a discussion. Turn this on and Flarum answers them — each old topic, tag and profile URL sends people to wherever that content ended up, with a permanent redirect so search engines move the ranking across instead of dropping it.
redirects.loading: Checking what this forum has to redirect…
redirects.no_runs: Nothing to redirect yet. Once an import has finished, this is where you point the old forum's addresses at their new homes.
redirects.source_help: Usually the platform you imported from. Change it if the links out in the world came from an earlier one — vBulletin 3, 4 and 5 all import the same way but serve completely different URLs.
redirects.unknown_source: No address patterns are known for that platform, so there is nothing to match against.
redirects.examples_intro: Real addresses from your import, resolved right now — these are exactly what visitors will get:
redirects.no_examples: This import's map has nothing to preview.
redirects.note: Only ever runs on a page Flarum could not answer itself, so it can never take over an address your forum already serves. Nothing is rewritten and nothing is stored — old links are matched as they arrive.
redirects.error_empty_map: That import has no id map left — it was reset, so there is nothing to look anything up in.
redirects.error_unknown_source: No address patterns are known for that platform.
redirects.error_failed: Could not save. Please try again.

pm.help: Conversations between two members become their Messages conversation. Conversations with three or more people come across as group conversations when Group Messages is installed. Only the people in a conversation can see it.
pm.no_groups: Group Messages is not installed, so conversations with three or more people will be skipped and counted. Install it first to bring them across too.
pm.unavailable: Private messages can be brought across once the Messages extension is enabled.

api.busy: Import #{id} is still running. Let it finish (or reset it) before starting another.

sync.no_base: There is no finished import to sync. Run an import first.
sync.unsupported: Syncing is not available for {source} yet. Its import still works; run it again into a fresh forum to pick up new content.
sync.needs_password: The source database password is not kept after a run. Enter it again to sync.
sync.needs_connection: This import is from before connection settings were kept, so enter the old forum's database details again (the same ones as the import).
sync.needs_upload: This import came from an uploaded file. Upload a fresh dump of the old forum to sync from it.
sync.summary: Synced {topics} new discussions, {posts} new posts, {users} new members, {edited} edited posts ({kept} edits kept because the post was changed here).

pm.groups_skipped: {count} group conversations skipped: install Group Messages to bring them across, then sync.
pm.unavailable: Private messages skipped: Messages is not enabled.

api.sqlsrv_missing: This server cannot connect to SQL Server directly: the PHP extension pdo_sqlsrv is not installed. Export the source database to a dump or CSV and use the file-upload import instead.
api.dump_unreadable: Could not open the uploaded dump.
api.scratch_failed: Could not create a scratch database at {path}

explain.timed_out: This server could not reach the source database at all: the connection timed out. The source MySQL server is not accepting connections from this server — usually a firewall blocking port 3306, MySQL listening on 127.0.0.1 only (bind-address), or the host not allowing remote MySQL (on cPanel, add this server's IP under Remote MySQL). If you cannot open it up, upload a dump instead, or load the dump into a database on this server and connect to 127.0.0.1.
explain.no_answer: Nothing answered at that host and port. Check the host and port, and that the database server is running and reachable from this server.
explain.host_refused: The source database refused this server's address. Grant the database user access from this server's IP (not just localhost).
explain.bad_login: The source database rejected the username or password. If they are right, the user may only be allowed to connect from localhost.

not_source.phpbb: This doesn't look like a phpBB database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix.
not_source.vbulletin: This doesn't look like a vBulletin database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix.
not_source.vbulletin5: This doesn't look like a vBulletin 5 database (missing “{table}”).
not_source.mybb: This doesn't look like a MyBB database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix.
not_source.smf: This doesn't look like an SMF database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix.
not_source.vanilla: This doesn't look like a Vanilla database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix.
not_source.invision: This doesn't look like an Invision Community database (missing “{table}”).
not_source.xenforo: This doesn't look like a XenForo database (missing “{table}”).
not_source.convoro: This doesn't look like a Convoro database (missing “{table}”).
not_source.convoro_columns: This database has the right table names but not Convoro's columns — is it really a Convoro forum?
not_source.discourse: This doesn't look like a Discourse database (missing “{table}”). Discourse uses PostgreSQL.
not_source.nodebb: This doesn't look like a NodeBB Redis store (no “global” or “categories:cid” key). Check the host, port and database number.
not_source.webwiz: This doesn't look like a Web Wiz Forums database (missing “{table}”). Check the table prefix — Web Wiz ships tables as tblAuthor, tblForum, tblTopic, tblThread.
not_source.webwiz_columns: Found the Web Wiz tables, but could not identify these columns: {columns}. This is likely a Web Wiz version with a different schema — send the output of a column listing for tblAuthor/tblForum/tblTopic/tblThread so the mapping can be extended.

nodebb.no_extension: Importing from NodeBB requires the PHP “redis” (phpredis) extension on the server.
nodebb.no_connect: Could not connect to the NodeBB Redis server at {host}:{port}.

upload.no_file: No file was uploaded (or it exceeded the server upload limit).
upload.too_large: That file is {size} — the limit is {limit}. Gzip the dump (.sql.gz) or import from a live database connection instead.
upload.wrong_source: File loaded, but it doesn't look like a {source} database: {error}
upload.skipped_batches: {skipped} of {total} row batches in this dump could not be read and were skipped, so some content may be missing. Importing from a live database connection avoids this.
upload.binary: That file doesn't look like a database dump — it appears to be binary. Upload a .sql, .sql.gz or SQLite file.
